title: how to support auto research in sepo?

nodes.body:
I reviewed both sides. My take: Sepo is close, but it does **not yet support `autoresearch` as a first-class loop**. The missing piece is not more agent capability; it is a deterministic experiment/result state machine.

`autoresearch`’s core algorithm is:

1. constrain the editable surface to one/few files;
2. run a fixed-budget experiment;
3. extract one objective metric;
4. keep the change only if the metric improves;
5. otherwise discard/revert;
6. repeat indefinitely or until an external budget stops it.

That is visible in `autoresearch`’s design: one editable file and fixed evaluator in [`README.md`](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch/blob/228791fb499afffb54b46200aca536f79142f117/README.md#L11-L17), fixed five-minute metric-based training in [`README.md`](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch/blob/228791fb499afffb54b46200aca536f79142f117/README.md#L61-L65), and the explicit keep/discard loop in [`program.md`](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch/blob/228791fb499afffb54b46200aca536f79142f117/program.md#L90-L112).

Sepo already has most orchestration primitives:

- bounded `implement -> review -> fix-pr -> review` handoff on `main`: [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L409-L616)
- planner-backed `/orchestrate` with runtime validation and max rounds: [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L3-L12)
- sub-orchestrators for splitting long work into child issues: [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L86-L127)
- stacked child work via `base_pr`: [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L103-L147)

The self-approval/self-merge stack adds the missing “accept and close the loop” mechanics, but note the current branch state: #180 is merged into the stacked self-approval branch, not flattened into `main`; #208 was closed as mis-stacked; the cleaned simplified self-merge version is #214. In that stack, approval and merge routing look like this: [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/agent/implement-issue-213/codex-25689072367/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L462-L513). The deterministic merge resolver checks current-head Sepo approval, checks, mergeability, and then merges or enables auto-merge: [`self-merge.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/agent/implement-issue-213/codex-25689072367/.agent/src/self-merge.ts#L196-L307), [`resolve-self-merge.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/agent/implement-issue-213/codex-25689072367/.agent/src/cli/resolve-self-merge.ts#L56-L202).

Recommended plan:

1. Land/settle the self-approval + simplified self-merge stack first. The auto-research loop depends on `review SHIP -> self-approve -> self-merge` being reliable.

2. Add a `ResearchSpec` parser and status model, probably in `.agent/src/research.ts`. The spec should live in the issue body or a repo file and include: editable paths, command, timeout, metric extraction rule, optimize direction, baseline score, best score, max iterations, and optional resource labels.

3. Add a deterministic result resolver CLI. This should parse run logs/artifacts, extract the metric, compare against the stored best score, and emit conclusions like `improved`, `regressed`, `crashed`, `inconclusive`, `budget_exhausted`. Do not let the LLM decide whether the metric improved.

4. Add a new experiment action, likely `agent-research-experiment.yml`, with a matching prompt. This is the `autoresearch` equivalent of “modify `train.py`, run `uv run train.py`, record result.” It should use explicit structured outputs and keep workflow glue thin, following existing Sepo patterns.

5. Extend orchestrator transitions with a new action type, probably `research-experiment`:
   - `/orchestrate` on a research issue -> `research-experiment`
   - `research-experiment: improved` -> `review`
   - `review: SHIP` -> `agent-self-approve`
   - `agent-self-approve: approved` -> `agent-self-merge`
   - `agent-self-merge: merged/auto_merge_enabled` -> next `research-experiment`
   - `research-experiment: regressed/crashed` -> next `research-experiment` with handoff context summarizing what failed
   - budget exhausted or repeated inconclusive results -> visible stop

6. Add a durable experiment ledger. For v1, I would use marker-upserted issue comments plus workflow artifacts, not memory. Memory is slow-changing project context; experiment metrics are run state. The ledger should mirror `results.tsv`: commit/PR, metric, memory/resource summary, status, description.

7. Add focused tests around: spec parsing, metric extraction, improvement comparison, crash handling, handoff routing, dedupe markers, max-round/budget stops, and self-merge continuation.

I would implement this as a new stacked slice after #214, not by overloading `implement` or `review`. The key product boundary is: agents propose experiment changes, deterministic code measures and accepts/rejects, and the existing review/self-approval/self-merge path handles code-quality and merge safety.

If this direction sounds right, approve a first implementation slice for `ResearchSpec + metric resolver + docs` before wiring the full workflow loop.

@sepo-agent /answer 

I think a more fundamental issue is this: 

> Extend orchestrator transitions with a new action type, probably research-experiment:
> 
> /orchestrate on a research issue -> research-experiment
> research-experiment: improved -> review
> review: SHIP -> agent-self-approve
> agent-self-approve: approved -> agent-self-merge
> agent-self-merge: merged/auto_merge_enabled -> next research-experiment
> research-experiment: regressed/crashed -> next research-experiment with handoff context summarizing what failed
> budget exhausted or repeated inconclusive results -> visible stop

I think the key challenge is to support a structured way for running (computational) experiment? 

1. Right now we have a code self-evolving loop: adding more features, review , fix-pr, self-approve . Issue is the main way of tracking this. 
2. Also we need to have an experiment self-evolving loop, and there are some key design challenges:
    - Where to manage the experiments?  Perhaps We can use discussion (with threads) to track experiments: 
        - One discussion page denotes one collection of experiments 
        - In each comment, it will write down the experiment setup, and it will update the results when it finishes 
        - And later when it finishes, it will comment in the thread about the summary of this current step and plan for the next steps 
        - Question: how to handle parallel exploration? 
    - What is the code infrastructure to run experiments and ?  
        - Shall we consider using slurm?
            - in that sense, it definitely needs a local runner that can connect to slurm?  also is https://github.com/celerity/slurmactiond related? 
            - moreover, what is the proper way to handle long-running jobs? the first simplest thing is to babysit all the experiment runs and then stop the action runs. But that only works for a limited time? 
        - Where to save experiment files? Saving in a different branch? Or saving using git-ref logs? Or saving using huggingface datasets?

Yes, I agree: the fundamental missing abstraction is **not** another orchestrator edge. It is a first-class **computational experiment** object with lifecycle, storage, compute backend, result parsing, and concurrency semantics.

The orchestrator should route experiment work, but it should not *be* the experiment system.

Current Sepo already has useful pieces:

- Issues are the current durable work unit for orchestration and sub-orchestration: [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L86-L127).
- Discussions are already supported as a posting surface, including threaded replies: [`respond.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/respond.ts#L56-L64), [`discussion.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/discussion.ts#L36-L57).
- Sepo has branch-backed memory/state patterns, but memory is for durable project context, not high-volume experiment logs: [`memory.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/architecture/memory.md#L1-L20).
- Current task timeouts are route-level and capped at 360 minutes in Sepo: [`task-timeout-policy.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/task-timeout-policy.ts#L1-L17). GitHub’s own current limits are 6 hours for GitHub-hosted jobs and 5 days for self-hosted jobs, so long experiments need an external job lifecycle rather than “keep the Action open forever”: [GitHub Actions limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/hosting-your-own-runners/managing-self-hosted-runners/usage-limits-for-self-hosted-runners).

Recommended model:

- **Issue = experiment program / controller**
  - Owns the objective, budget, metric, allowed code area, compute backend, and current best result.
  - This should remain the orchestrator target because access policy, route dispatch, sub-orchestration, and state recovery already work there.

- **Discussion = lab notebook / human-readable experiment collection**
  - One discussion can represent a collection of experiments.
  - Each top-level comment can represent one trial or lane.
  - Replies can hold status updates, final result, and next-step reasoning.
  - But discussion comments should not be the only source of truth. Use hidden markers plus structured state in a branch/ref so parallel lanes do not race by editing prose.

- **PR/branch = accepted code candidate**
  - If an experiment changes code, the code lives on a branch/PR.
  - Improved candidates can go through review/self-approval/self-merge.
  - Failed or regressed candidates can be closed, discarded, or left as archived evidence.

- **Artifact/object store = experiment payloads**
  - Small logs/metrics: GitHub Actions artifacts and compact discussion summaries.
  - Structured run records: a dedicated branch like `agent/experiments` or ref-backed JSON state, not `agent/memory`.
  - Large files/checkpoints/datasets: external storage such as Hugging Face Datasets, S3/R2/GCS, or a lab filesystem. Store only URI, checksum, metric, and provenance in GitHub.

For parallel exploration, I would model each trial as:

```text
experiment_collection_id
trial_id
lane_id
parent_trial_id?
status: queued | submitted | running | succeeded | failed | cancelled
code_ref
job_id
metric
artifact_uri
summary
```

Then the reducer deterministically decides whether a completed trial becomes the new best. Multiple lanes can run in parallel, but only the reducer updates `best_score` / `best_trial_id`. That avoids “last comment wins” races.

On compute infrastructure:

- **Short jobs** can run directly on a self-hosted runner.
- **Long jobs** should use submit/poll/finalize:
  1. `experiment-submit` creates a Slurm/local/cloud job and records `job_id`.
  2. The GitHub Action exits.
  3. A scheduled or manually dispatched `experiment-poll` checks job state.
  4. `experiment-finalize` collects logs/artifacts, parses metrics, updates discussion/state, and asks the orchestrator for the next trial.

For Slurm specifically: yes, a local runner on or near the cluster head/login node is the right basic shape. `slurmactiond` is related but solves a slightly different layer: it receives GitHub webhooks and schedules ephemeral GitHub Actions runners through local `srun` on a Slurm head node: [celerity/slurmactiond README](https://github.com/celerity/slurmactiond#readme). That is useful if we want Actions jobs themselves to run inside Slurm allocations. For Sepo experiments, I would start simpler: a stable self-hosted runner with `sbatch`, `squeue`/`sacct`, `scancel`, and artifact collection access. Add slurmactiond later if dynamic runner allocation becomes important.

Implementation plan I would propose:

1. Add `ExperimentSpec` and `ExperimentRun` schemas plus parser/formatter CLIs.
2. Add discussion-backed notebook helpers: create collection, create trial comment, update trial result, reply with next-step plan.
3. Add a local command adapter for short experiments.
4. Add a Slurm adapter with `submit`, `poll`, `cancel`, and `collect`.
5. Add deterministic metric parsing and best-result reduction.
6. Add orchestrator integration after the experiment lifecycle is stable.
7. Add storage provider hooks for large artifacts.

So the first coding slice should **not** be `research-experiment -> review`. It should be: **structured experiment state + discussion notebook + deterministic result lifecycle**, with a local adapter first. Then Slurm and parallel lanes become clean extensions.

@sepo-agent /answer 

Speaking of this, does our current (meta) orchestrator support planning based on the outcome of the previous PRs? for example, 
1. if the previous self-approve decides to start a new PR (and dropping the older), can it support that? 
2. for the meta orchestrator, after we implement the experiment runner, can it replan experiments based on the previous experiment running resutls?

Short answer: **partially, but not enough for the two cases you described.**

Current orchestrator supports replanning from prior outcomes in a limited GitHub-native way:

- Each handoff carries `source_action`, `source_conclusion`, optional `next_target_number`, and optional `source_handoff_context`: [`dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts#L59-L78).
- The planner prompt sees that context: [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L6-L16).
- The meta-orchestrator can resume after a child finishes, post a parent progress comment, and dispatch the parent issue orchestrator again: [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L987-L1057).
- The planner can then choose `delegate_issue`, `implement`, `review`, `fix-pr`, `stop`, or `blocked`, within runtime policy: [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L468-L615).

But the current model is still mostly **workflow outcome based**, not **structured result based**.

For case 1: **“previous self-approve decides to start a new PR and drop the older one”**

Not currently supported as a first-class transition.

On `main`, the allowed concrete actions are only `implement`, `review`, and `fix-pr`: [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L3-L4). PR-level orchestration is explicitly restricted to `review` or `fix-pr`, not `implement` or `delegate_issue`: [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L555-L577). The prompt says the same: [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L80-L82).

So a PR-local self-approval workflow cannot currently say: “close this PR, go back to the parent issue, create a replacement PR.” The nearest existing pattern is meta-orchestration: a child can finish as failed/blocked/done, then the parent issue planner can delegate another child. But even there, the current parent resume only passes a prose `request_text` summary, not a structured “supersede PR #X with new attempt Y” payload: [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1038-L1054).

To support this cleanly, I would add a deterministic **supersede** concept:

```text
self-approve/requested-replacement
  -> parent issue replan
  -> close or mark old PR superseded
  -> create replacement child/PR
```

That should be explicit runtime behavior, not just an LLM instruction. It needs fields like `superseded_pr`, `reason`, `replacement_base`, and `carry_forward_context`.

For case 2: **“after experiment runner, can meta orchestrator replan based on previous experiment results?”**

Conceptually yes, but not with the current state shape.

The meta-orchestrator can already replan after child completion. That is the right control loop. What is missing is a structured experiment result payload. Today the parent gets a child outcome like `done`, `blocked`, or `failed`, plus a summary string: [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L998-L1027). That is enough for code-task orchestration, but too weak for experiments.

For experiment replanning, the parent needs something like:

```json
{
  "trial_id": "exp-012",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "metric": 0.9871,
  "direction": "minimize",
  "baseline_metric": 0.9910,
  "improved": true,
  "artifact_uri": "...",
  "code_ref": "...",
  "notes": "larger batch improved bpb but used +8GB VRAM"
}
```

Then the meta planner can make a real next-trial decision instead of scraping comments.

Recommended change:

1. Add an `experiment-result` schema and deterministic parser.
2. Let experiment actions return `source_handoff_context` containing the structured result or a pointer to it.
3. Update terminal child-to-parent reporting to pass structured result context, not only prose `request_text`.
4. Extend allowed planner decisions for experiment issues: `run_experiment`, `supersede_trial`, `promote_result`, `stop`.
5. Keep deterministic comparison outside the LLM: metric improved/regressed should be computed by code, while the planner proposes the next idea.

So the answer is:

- **Current orchestrator can replan from coarse previous outcomes.**
- **It cannot yet make robust decisions from rich prior PR/experiment results.**
- **It also cannot currently replace/drop an old PR as a first-class action.**
- **For experiments, we should add structured result state and a supersede/promote lifecycle before wiring more transitions.**
